title: Kestrel Consortium — inference security onboarding scout
summary: Initial security posture discovery focused on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment choices, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO attestations, retention and audit log expectations. Customer wants a path for a low-friction pilot but also strong controls for regulated data and key ownership. Agreed next steps include sending SOC2 pack, KMS integration notes, and scheduling a SE-led deep technical runbook and on-prem proof-of-concept timeline.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM), Liam, Priya, Carlos, Nina (Kestrel)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Maya our solutions engineer. how're you all doing?
[00:06] Liam: Good, thanks. excited to understand where Redwood fits. we run a multi-tenant platform, lots of regulated customers, so security is the big gating factor.
[00:12] Priya: yeah hi i'm priya, security lead. our main asks are SOC2 compliance evidence, SSO integration via our SAML IdP, and strict key control. we need to know about KMS and HSM options, and whether we can bring our own keys.
[00:24] Maya: absolutely. high level — Redwood supports hosted API for the quickest path, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictability, and Private (VPC / on-prem) for full isolation. for keys we have managed KMS options and BYOK patterns that can integrate with customer KMS/HSMs.
[00:36] Nina: when you say BYOK, do you mean we can use our cloud KMS with customer-controlled keys or you require key escrow?
[00:43] Maya: good question. we support a few modes: platform-managed keys, customer-managed keys in supported cloud KMSes (aws/kms, gcp/kms), and a dedicated HSM option for private deployments. for hosted we offer envelope encryption with our service wrapping, but you can push control by bringing your key — that results in Redwood never having the plaintext key. caveat: some features like cross-region fallback need additional config.
[01:05] Carlos: is there an HSM connector for on-prem HSMs? we run a Thales cluster and need FIPS and HSM-backed key ops.
[01:11] Maya: we have integrations patterns for external HSMs — for Private deployments we can connect to customer HSMs via a gateway. we'd want to validate the exact vendor and API, but that's supported in our enterprise offering.
[01:20] Priya: data residency: our contracts require retention control and the ability to delete logs and model prompts on request. how granular is the retention control?
[01:28] Samir: you can configure retention windows per workspace, and we provide deletion APIs plus audit logs to prove deletion. for Hosted accounts we retain telemetry for 90 days by default but that's configurable with an enterprise retention add-on.
[01:40] Liam: audit logs — what's included? api keys usage, token-level traces, prompt redaction?
[01:46] Maya: audit logs capture request metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model, route), auth events (login, token create/delete), and admin actions (role assignments, key rotations). we do not log full prompt text by default unless enabled for debugging — that is controlled and can be redacted. there is an optional secure logging path to ship logs to your SIEM (splunk/elk) and retain them according to your policy.
[02:05] Priya: okay makes sense. SOC2 / ISO — can you provide your current report? and do you have scope notes about encryption in transit and at rest?
[02:12] Samir: yes we'll send the SOC2 Type II report and the ISO27001 certificate summary. quick note, Hosted environments are in scope for Redwood's SOC2; Private on-prem customers usually manage their own attestations for the infra they control but we help with evidence for our control plane.
[02:28] Carlos: how do you separate customer data in Dedicated? is it logical multi-tenancy or physical isolation?
[02:34] Maya: Dedicated is logically isolated within a reserved GPU pool — namespaces are strongly separated, with tenant-level RBAC and network policies. for physical isolation we recommend Private deployments. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and dedicated capacity, but not physical racks.
[02:48] Nina: SSO — we need SAML 2.0 with SCIM for user provisioning, and granular RBAC so engineers only see the projects they own.
[02:56] Samir: we support SAML SSO, OIDC, SCIM provisioning for users and groups, and RBAC with role templates. you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles and even create custom roles for fine-grained perms.
[03:08] Priya: what about admin logs and who can request key rotation? we need separation of duties — ops can rotate keys but not read service logs, and security can view logs but not rotate keys.
[03:17] Maya: RBAC supports role scoping: admin roles for ops, security observer roles with read-only audit log access, and a key-manager role. we can demo an example policy during the SE deep-dive.
[03:26] Liam: threat model — if someone exfiltrates model prompts, what mitigations exist?
[03:31] Maya: several layers: transport encryption (TLS 1.2+), envelope encryption for data at rest, per-tenant key material, and optional prompt redaction before storage. plus we have detection alerts for anomalous request patterns and can route suspicious traffic to a quarantine queue. our recommended pattern for high-risk customers is Private with customer-managed keys and no persistent prompt storage.
[03:52] Carlos: performance tradeoffs with envelope encryption? any latency hit?
[03:56] Maya: minimal — key unwrap/rewrap adds a few ms typically, depends on HSM latency and network hops. for Dedicated we can colocate KMS endpoints to reduce round trip. we also support caching of DEKs for live sessions to reduce HSM calls.
[04:10] Priya: compliance evidence — you mentioned sending the SOC2. do you also have architecture diagrams, control mappings (eg, mapping to NIST or ISO controls), and pen test reports?
[04:18] Samir: yes we'll share the SOC2, a controls mapping matrix and our latest pen test executive summary. full pen test artefacts require an NDA in some cases but we can share summaries and remediation timelines.
[04:30] Nina: curious about data deletion proofs — can you provide cryptographic proof or an audit that data was removed?
[04:37] Maya: we provide deletion logs and request IDs that you can cross-check. for Private deployments where you manage storage, you can run your own verification. cryptographic deletion proofs are non-trivial, but we've built deletion attestations into our compliance pack — timestamps, request IDs, and operator signatures.
[04:54] Priya: what about logs retention and exporting to our SIEM?
[04:57] Maya: we can stream audit logs via secure forwarders to your SIEM, with options for syslog over TLS, S3 export with SSE-KMS, or direct API push. retention is controlled on the destination SIEM side; we can also maintain a shorter audit retention in Redwood if you want a lightweight copy.
[05:14] Carlos: do you have a recommended pilot path? we want to try with non-prod data and validate RBAC, KMS flows, and audit exports.
[05:20] Jordan: recommended pilot: a 2-week Dedicated sandbox with a single reserved pool, KMS enabled with customer-managed keys (test keys), SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning, and audit log streaming to your staging Splunk instance. SE will run a checklist of controls.
[05:33] Priya: timeline — we have a board decision in early january, need vendor risk docs this month.
[05:38] Samir: understood — we'll prioritize SOC2/ISO artifacts and the security on-boarding playbook. we'll aim to get those to you by next week.
[05:45] Liam: one more — data residency: can tokens be restricted to EU only? some of our customers require EU data at rest.
[05:51] Maya: yes, location routing is supported. Hosted can pin workloads to EU regions, Dedicated can be provisioned in EU-only zones, and Private obviously gives full control over physical location. there are SLA differences and possibly higher costs for region-restricted capacity.
[06:05] Priya: any emergency access policies? we're concerned about vendor employees having break-glass access.
[06:10] Maya: break-glass is tightly controlled, requires two-person approval, is fully logged, and we can exclude certain namespaces from vendor-admin access if needed. for Private deployments, vendor access can be disabled completely.
[06:22] Carlos: do you offer encryption at field-level or structured PII redaction?
[06:26] Maya: we offer pre-ingest redaction and redaction templates. field-level encryption is supported in Private deployments where you can bring your own crypto libraries, otherwise we do column-level encryption patterns.
[06:37] Priya: ok that helps. can we see a sample RBAC policy?
[06:40] Maya: yes, we'll attach a sample role matrix.
[06:43] Samir: wrapping up: next steps: we'll send the SOC2 and ISO artifacts, Maya will send KMS/HSM integration details and an RBAC sample, Jordan will schedule the SE deep-dive and the Dedicated pilot calendar. Priya will share Kestrel's retention matrix and legal risk questions.
[06:58] Priya: perfect. thanks everyone. look forward to the artifacts.
[07:02] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up by email with links.

Notes: transcription has some name mismatches and occasional misheard words (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated). References shared: SOC2 pack link (sent later), KMS integration doc (link to be shared), RBAC sample spreadsheet (to be attached). SE deep-dive tentatively week of 2026-12-06.
